# Triage report: alt_0001, Office application spawned PowerShell

## Summary

A Word document started encoded PowerShell (evt_004047), which downloaded and ran msupdate.exe (evt_004052). The payload then beaconed to a known-bad host (evt_004054). The verdict is malicious.

## Triage decision

**P2, endpoint.** Word started encoded PowerShell, and its anomaly score is high.

## Intel brief

The child msupdate.exe has a known-bad hash and the domain is known bad. Word and PowerShell themselves are known-good binaries.

| trigger | powershell.exe | Microsoft Windows | known_good | evt_004047 |
| child | msupdate.exe | unsigned | known_bad | evt_004052 |

## Verdict and risk

**Verdict: malicious** (confidence 0.90).
F1 to F5 show a document starting a downloader that beacons to a known-bad host (F6). Nothing confirmed supports the harmless hypothesis.

**Risk score: 73 / 100**

## Limitations

- The agent recommends and a human decides; nothing in this report was executed.
- Code refuses a benign verdict if any indicator in the case is known_bad or any log text has an injection flag, and requires a confirmed finding tied to the trigger, its parent or children, or an entity in the intel brief. It cannot check that the finding really supports the harmless explanation: the model picks which finding counts.
- Citation checks confirm that an event involves the entity named and that the acting process matches. They cannot confirm every other detail of a claim.
- Not ruled on by the reviewer: F6.
- The ATT&CK validator refused 1 proposal(s): T1999 is not a technique in ATT&CK v20
- Dropped isolate_host on PROD-DB-99: its target is not an entity in this case.
